Standard: Clamping of hydraulic and pneumatic tubing and hoses is IAW SAE AS5440B, Tubing Support paragraph and Hose Support paragraph. This includes clamping types, location of clamps, spacing, and identifying natural frequencies of installed tubing. Tubing and its supporting hardware are not used to provide support of other air vehicle installations, such as wiring, other air vehicle tubing (e.g., fuel and air lines), or similar installations. Where hydraulic tubes of different diameters are connected, spacing of the smallest tube diameter will be used. Marriage or butterfly clamps attached between hydraulic or pneumatic tubing may be used to maintain clearance, but not for support of such tubes. Marriage or butterfly clamps attached between hydraulic or pneumatic tubing and other system lines, such as wiring, other air vehicle tubing, or similar installations are prohibited. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review system-level drawings, processes (manufacturers process specifications), and CAD models to verify that the hydraulic and pneumatic system design meets specified clamp spacing, has provisions for tubing expansion and contraction, and lines are not attached via clamps to other tubing, wiring, or components.
(2) Review results of a quality assessment or a government in-person sampling of physical inspection(s) (e.g., 30-60-90% of build inspections) of the air vehicle to verify hydraulic and pneumatic lines are clamped IAW the standard. Analysis.
  (1) Review analysis to verify natural frequencies of tube installations are identified and that no resonant frequencies exist with surrounding air vehicle structure and systems. Test.
    (1) Ground test: Conduct RAP testing on installed tubing for critical systems to verify the analysis and that no resonant frequencies exist with surrounding air vehicle structure and systems.
